gaps: Static dtype, six-rank default capacity, incomplete operator/indexing semantics, and unverified complete scalar-operation coverage. Native float32 full/axis products, axis means and cumulative sums/products cover scoped negative/scalar axes and empty/noncontiguous/broadcast reads. CPU float64 whole/axis sums/products/means and ordered scans have packed kernels, strided fallbacks and tight-tolerance seeded VJP observations; this is scoped numerical coverage, not every reduction option. CPU integer/bool whole/axis sums/products and cumulative sums/products promote to int64 before modulo-2^64 arithmetic, including uint64 upper-half bit patterns. CPU real-valued sums, products, means and cumulative sums/products accept explicit float32/float64 output dtypes and cast on read with numeric unsigned conversion; means reject omitted integer/bool dtypes. Floating scans retain ordered float64 carries and casted scalar signs; products multiply in the requested dtype. CPU explicit uint8 and signed integer output sums/products/scans wrap modulo their dtype; bool sums/products are logical OR/AND. Wider unsigned reductions accept only empty inputs; bool and wider unsigned scans accept scalars and empties. Means reject integer/bool output dtypes, and floating-to-integer observations stay within the documented defined cast range. CPU complex sums, products, means and scans accept explicit complex outputs from real/bool/complex inputs and real outputs from complex inputs; numeric sum/product/scan casts and scalar/empty exceptions are covered. CPU amin/amax preserve bool, uint8, signed integer, float32 and float64 dtypes across whole/single/multiple axes, keepdim and strided views. Pinned ARM64 observations cover extrema NaN/signed-zero folds, scalar/empty validation and unsupported dtype exceptions; CPU float32/float64 seeded first-order extrema VJPs cover equal ties, nonfinite masks, signed/broadcast inputs, strided seeds and retained signed-zero contributions; extrema out=, half/bfloat16, higher-order autograd and Metal remain gaps. CPU argmin/argmax return independent int64 indices for supported floating, signed integer and uint8 inputs, with squeezed defaults, keepdim, first logical ties/NaNs and strided reads. Bool/complex rejection and wider unsigned scalar/singleton/empty dispatch exceptions are covered; index out=, half/bfloat16 and Metal implementations remain gaps. CPU paired minWithIndices/maxWithIndices return independent input-dtype values and int64 indices, supporting bool, signed strides, first source zero/NaN bits and negative axes. Paired wider unsigned kernels accept rank-zero scalars and empty outputs but reject nonempty singleton dimensions; paired complex dtype rejection follows axis and empty-axis validation. CPU paired float32/float64 values support seeded first-index scatter gradients without tie splitting or nonfinite mask arithmetic. Paired out=, half/bfloat16, higher-order autograd and Metal remain gaps. Mixed-dtype autograd and Metal dtype options remain gaps. Metal scans use grouped float32 arithmetic with ordered range-sensitive product chains. Seeded first-order product-scan VJPs support CPU float32/float64 and native Metal float32. Other reduction dtype/out options, integer Metal reductions/scans, integer autograd and other operator-promotion contracts remain outside this slice. This is not the full reduction/operator surface.
